results.title: Perron's irreducibility criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f = x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0$ be a monic polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n \ge 1$ with $a_0 \neq 0$ and $|a_{n-1}| > 1 + \sum_{i=0}^{n-2} |a_i|$. Then $f$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Irreducibility of polynomials with coefficients in an arithmetic progression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ and let $a$, $d$ be coprime positive integers with $m^2 d^2 < 8a$. Then the polynomial $a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + (m - 1)d) x + (a + md)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: The arithmetic-progression quartic is not a product of two quadratics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $d$ be coprime integers with $0 < d \le a$. Then the polynomial $a x^4 + (a + d) x^3 + (a + 2d) x^2 + (a + 3d) x + (a + 4d)$ is not the product of two polynomials of degree $2$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Irreducibility when $d$ has a primitive-root prime factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ with $m + 1$ prime, and let $a$, $d$ be coprime positive integers. Suppose $d$ has a prime divisor $p$ that is not divisible by $m + 1$ and whose residue modulo $m + 1$ has multiplicative order $m$ (that is, $p$ is a primitive root modulo $m + 1$). Then the polynomial $a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + (m - 1)d) x + (a + md)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: The auxiliary equation has a unique positive root, which exceeds $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ and let $a$, $d$ be integers with $0 < d \le a$. Then the equation $a x^{m+2} + (a - d) x^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) x - (a + md) = 0$ has exactly one positive real solution, and every positive real solution $x$ satisfies $x > 1$.

results.title: Bound on the zeros of the arithmetic-progression polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$ be integers with $0 < d \le a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with $a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then every complex zero $z$ of $A_m(x) = a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + md)$ satisfies $|z| \le \lambda$, and $|z| = \lambda$ only if $z = -\lambda$.

results.title: Lower bound on a power of the auxiliary root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$ be integers with $0 < d \le a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with $a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then $a + md < a \lambda^m$.

results.title: Strict upper bound on floors at powers of the auxiliary root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$ be natural numbers with $d > 0$ and $(m + 1)d < 2a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with $a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then $\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor < a + pd$ for every integer $p$ with $1 \le p \le m - 1$.

results.title: Exact floor at a power of the auxiliary root (single exponent)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$ be positive integers, and let $p$ be an integer with $1 \le p \le m - 1$ and $p(m - p)d^2 < 2a$. If $\lambda > 0$ is a real number with $a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$, then $\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor = a + pd - 1$.

results.title: Exact floors at powers of the auxiliary root (all exponents)

Then $\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor = a + pd - 1$ for every integer $p$ with $1 \le p \le m - 1$.

results.title: Double root criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. Then $f(a) = 0$ and $f'(a) = 0$ if and only if $f = (x - a)^2 g$ for some $g \in R[x]$.

results.title: Double root criterion in divisibility form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. Then $(x - a)^2$ divides $f$ in $R[x]$ if and only if $f(a) = 0$ and $f'(a) = 0$.

results.title: A nonvanishing derivative excludes a double root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. If $f'(a) \neq 0$, then $(x - a)^2$ does not divide $f$ in $R[x]$.

results.title: Integer solutions of a sum of squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the solution set is the set of all integer vectors $x = (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.

results.title: Representation numbers of sums of squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the representation number $r_k(n)$ is the number of elements of the solution set, that is, the number of integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$. Representations that differ in the order or the signs of the entries are counted separately.

results.title: Finitely many representations as a sum of squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, there are only finitely many integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.

results.title: The representation number counts a finite set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the representation number $r_k(n)$ equals the number of elements of the finite solution set of integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.

results.title: The zero vector represents zero as a sum of squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the zero vector of $\mathbb{Z}^k$ has squared norm $0$, that is, it lies in the set of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = 0$.

results.title: Solution set of the empty sum at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The set of vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $0$ is all of $\mathbb{Z}^0$.

results.title: Zero squares never sum to a positive integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, no vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ has sum of squares equal to $n$; that is, the solution set is empty.

results.title: Solution set of one square equal to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The set of vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ with $x_1^2 = 0$ consists of the zero vector alone.

results.title: Zero as a sum of zero squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The representation number $r_0(0)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $0$, is $1$.

results.title: Positive integers have no representation as a sum of zero squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the representation number $r_0(n)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $n$, is $0$.

results.title: Zero as a sum of one square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The representation number $r_1(0)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ with $x_1^2 = 0$, equals $1$.

results.title: Holomorphic maps on a connected manifold that agree on a nonempty open set are equal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a connected complex manifold without boundary, modeled on a complex normed space with complex $C^1$ (that is, holomorphic) transition maps, and let $F$ be a complex normed space. If two holomorphic (everywhere complex differentiable) maps $f, g : M \to F$ agree on a nonempty open subset $U \subseteq M$, then $f = g$.

results.title: Identity theorem for holomorphic maps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a connected complex manifold without boundary, modeled on a complex normed space with complex $C^1$ (that is, holomorphic) transition maps, and let $F$ be a complex normed space. If two holomorphic (everywhere complex differentiable) maps $f, g : M \to F$ agree on a nonempty open subset $U \subseteq M$, then $f = g$.

results.title: Open mapping theorem for one-dimensional complex manifolds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be complex manifolds without boundary modeled on complex normed spaces of dimension one, with complex $C^1$ (that is, holomorphic) transition maps, and suppose $M$ is connected. Then every holomorphic (everywhere complex differentiable) map $f : M \to N$ that is not constant is an open map.

results.title: Open mapping theorem for Riemann surfaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be complex manifolds without boundary modeled on complex normed spaces of dimension one, with complex $C^1$ (that is, holomorphic) transition maps, and suppose $M$ is connected. Then every holomorphic (everywhere complex differentiable) map $f : M \to N$ that is not constant is an open map.

results.title: Browder–Göhde–Kirk fixed point theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach space and let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set. If a map $f : E \to E$ sends $K$ into $K$ and is nonexpansive on $K$, that is, $\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, then $f$ has a fixed point in $K$: there is $y \in K$ with $f(y) = y$.

results.title: Diameter of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The diameter of a set $s$ in a real normed space is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $x, y \in s$; by the convention for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.

results.title: Radius of a point in a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The radius of a point $x$ in a set $s$ of a real normed space is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $y \in s$; by the convention for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.

results.title: Diametral point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A point $x$ of a real normed space is diametral in a set $s$ if $x \in s$ and the radius of $x$ in $s$ equals the diameter of $s$.

results.title: Normal structure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K$ in a real normed space has normal structure if every convex subset $H \subseteq K$ with at least two points contains a point that is not diametral in $H$.

results.title: Nonexpansive self-map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A map $T : K \to K$ from a subset $K$ of a real normed space to itself is nonexpansive if $\|T(x) - T(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, that is, if $T$ is $1$-Lipschitz for the distance inherited from the space.

results.title: Kirk's fixed-point theorem for sets with normal structure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a reflexive real Banach space, meaning that the canonical embedding of $E$ into its double dual is surjective, and let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set with normal structure. Then every nonexpansive self-map $T : K \to K$ has a fixed point.

results.title: The INVERT transform of an integer sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The INVERT transform of an integer sequence $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is the integer sequence $b = (b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in which $b_n$ is the coefficient of $x^{n+1}$ in the inverse of $1 - \sum_{m \ge 0} a_m x^{m+1}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$ (the inverse exists because the constant coefficient is $1$). In the one-based indexing of the source, $a_n$ and $b_n$ are the terms of index $n + 1$.

results.title: Generating function of the INVERT transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be an integer sequence and $b = (b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ its INVERT transform, and put $A(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n x^{n+1}$ and $B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} b_n x^{n+1}$. Then $(1 - A(x))(1 + B(x)) = 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$, that is, $1 + B(x)$ is the inverse of $1 - A(x)$.

results.title: Parent forest with a depth certificate
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A parent forest on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consists of a parent map $p$ from the vertices to themselves (a vertex $x$ with $p(x) = x$ is a root) and a depth certificate $d$ assigning a natural number to every vertex, such that every non-root edge strictly decreases the certificate: if $p(x) \ne x$, then $d(p(x)) < d(x)$.

results.title: Root of a vertex in a parent forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parent forest $F$ with parent map $p$ and a vertex $x$, the root of $x$ is found by following parent pointers from $x$: it is $x$ itself if $p(x) = x$, and otherwise it is the root of $p(x)$.

results.title: Path length to the root
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parent forest $F$ with parent map $p$ and a vertex $x$, the path length of $x$ is the number of parent edges followed from $x$ to its root: it is $0$ if $p(x) = x$, and otherwise one more than the path length of $p(x)$.

results.title: Find with cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, find with cost returns the root that find returns for $x$, together with the cost $\ell(x) + 1$, where $\ell(x)$ is the path length of $x$ (the number of non-root parent edges that find traverses from $x$). That is, it charges one unit for every visited vertex, including the root.

results.title: Equivalent vertices of a parent forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two vertices $x$ and $y$ of a parent forest $F$ are equivalent when find returns the same root for $x$ as for $y$ in $F$.

results.title: Find returns a root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the vertex $r$ that find returns for $x$ is a root of $F$: the parent of $r$ in $F$ is $r$ itself.

results.title: Find is unchanged along a parent pointer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, find returns the same root for the parent of $x$ in $F$ as for $x$.

results.title: Every vertex is equivalent to its representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the vertex $x$ is equivalent in $F$ to the root that find returns for $x$.

results.title: The cost of find is the path length plus one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the cost that find with cost charges on $x$ equals $\ell(x) + 1$, where $\ell(x)$ is the path length of $x$: the number of non-root parent edges that find traverses from $x$.

results.title: The cost of find is at most the depth certificate plus one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$ with depth certificate $d$, the cost that find with cost charges on $x$ is at most $d(x) + 1$.

results.title: Parent map after linking two roots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest with parent map $p$, and let $r$ and $s$ be vertices. The linked parent map sends $r$ to $s$ and agrees with $p$ on every other vertex: it maps $z$ to $s$ if $z = r$, and to $p(z)$ otherwise.

results.title: Depth certificate after linking two roots
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest with depth certificate $d$, and let $r$ and $s$ be vertices. The linked depth certificate assigns to a vertex $z$ the number $d(z) + d(s) + 1$ if $z$ is equivalent to $r$ in $F$ (that is, $z$ and $r$ have the same root), and $d(z)$ otherwise.

results.title: Representatives after a union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest, let $x, y, z$ be vertices of $F$, and let $F'$ be the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$. If $z$ is equivalent to $x$ in $F$, then find returns for $z$ in $F'$ the root that find returns for $y$ in $F$; otherwise find returns the same root for $z$ in $F'$ as in $F$.

results.title: Union makes its arguments equivalent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every parent forest $F$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the vertices $x$ and $y$ are equivalent in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Union of equivalent vertices changes nothing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $x$ and $y$ are equivalent vertices of a parent forest $F$, then the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ is $F$ itself.

results.title: Equivalence after a union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest and let $x, y, a, b$ be vertices of $F$. Then $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in $F$, or $a$ is equivalent to $x$ and $b$ is equivalent to $y$ in $F$, or $a$ is equivalent to $y$ and $b$ is equivalent to $x$ in $F$.

results.title: Union preserves the representatives of unrelated classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest and let $x, y, z$ be vertices of $F$. If $z$ is not equivalent to $x$ in $F$, then find returns the same root for $z$ in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$ as in $F$.

results.title: Union in a parent forest with cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parent forest $F$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the costed union returns the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ together with a cost equal to the cost of finding the root of $x$ plus the cost of finding the root of $y$ (each one unit per visited vertex, including the root), plus one more unit when the roots of $x$ and $y$ are distinct; when they coincide, union performs no link and none is charged.

results.title: Cost bound for union in a parent forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every parent forest $F$ with depth certificate $d$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the cost charged for the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ (two root searches at one unit per visited vertex, plus one unit for the link when the roots differ) is at most $d(x) + d(y) + 3$.

results.title: Correctness of the union-find equivalence query
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call two natural numbers $a$ and $c$ equivalent in a union-find structure when they have the same root, where a number that is not a node is its own root. Let $U$ be a union-find structure with nodes $0, \dots, N-1$ and let $x, y < N$. The equivalence query on $x$ and $y$, which runs FIND-SET with path compression on $x$ and then on $y$, returns a union-find structure $U'$ and a boolean $b$ such that $U'$ has $N$…

results.title: Connected components via union-find
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, CONNECTED-COMPONENTS first builds the union-find structure with $n$ singleton nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ by $n$ MAKE-SET calls. It then processes the pairs $(u, v)$ of $E$ in list order: it asks whether $u$ and $v$ are equivalent using two FIND-SET calls, keeping the path compression done by the query, and if they are not equivalent…

results.title: Connected components allocates $n$ nodes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $E$ of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the union-find structure returned by CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ has exactly $n$ nodes.

results.title: Connected components computes reachability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $E$ be a list of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For all vertices $a, b < n$, $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in the union-find structure returned by CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are joined by a path in the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ whose edges are the unordered pairs $\{u, v\}$ with $(u, v)$ in $E$ and $u \ne v$.

results.title: Operation counts of connected components
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $E$ be a list of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $m$ be the length of $E$. Let $G$ be the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ whose edges are the unordered pairs $\{u, v\}$ with $(u, v)$ in $E$ and $u \ne v$, and let $k$ be the number of connected components of $G$. Running CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ makes exactly $n$ MAKE-SET calls, $2m$ FIND-SET calls and…

results.title: Cost-counted FIND auxiliary
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ with node array $A$ and a node $x < |S|$, this is the recursive path-compression routine of FIND, paired with a cost in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$. It charges $(1, 0)$ for testing whether $x$ is a root. If the parent $y$ of $x$ in $A$ equals $x$, it returns $A$ and the root $x$. Otherwise it runs on $y$, obtaining an array $A'$ and a root $r$, charges $(0, 1)$ for one parent…

results.title: The cost-counted FIND auxiliary returns the uncounted result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, the value returned by the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ (the compressed node array together with the root of $x$), with its cost discarded, equals the result of the Batteries path-compression auxiliary routine of FIND on $x$.

results.title: Cost of the FIND auxiliary at a root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x < |S|$ a node. If the parent of $x$ in $S$ is $x$ itself, then the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ has cost $(1, 0)$: one root test and no parent writes.

results.title: Cost recurrence of the FIND auxiliary at a non-root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x < |S|$ a node whose parent $y$ in $S$ differs from $x$. If $c_x$ and $c_y$ are the costs of the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ and on $y$, then $c_x = (1, 0) + (c_y + (0, 1))$: one root test at $x$, then the run on $y$, then one parent write.

results.title: Root tests exceed parent writes by one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, if the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ has cost $(t, w)$, where $t$ counts root tests and $w$ counts parent writes, then $t = w + 1$.

results.title: Cost-counted FIND
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, this runs the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$, obtaining a node array $A'$, a root $r$ and a cost $(t, w)$. It returns the union-find structure with node array $A'$, together with $r$ as a node of that structure (whose size equals $|S|$), at cost $(t, w)$.

results.title: The cost-counted FIND returns the FIND result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, the value returned by the cost-counted FIND on $x$ (the compressed union-find structure together with the root of $x$), with its cost discarded, equals the result of the Batteries FIND with path compression on $x$.

results.title: Parent writes are bounded by the rank gap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, let $R$ be one more than the maximum rank of a node of $S$, and let $x < |S|$ be a node. The number of parent writes performed by the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ (the second coordinate of its cost) is at most $R - \operatorname{rank}(x)$.

results.title: FIND compresses exactly the original path to the root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure with parent map $p$ (where $p(i) = i$ for $i \ge |S|$), let $x < |S|$, and let $p'$ be the parent map of the structure produced by FIND with path compression on $x$. Then for every natural number $i$, $p'(i)$ is the root of $x$ if $i = p^k(x)$ for some $k \ge 0$, and $p'(i) = p(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: Effect of path-compressing find on each node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a union-find structure on the indices $0, \dots, n-1$ with parent function $p$, let $x < n$, and let $r$ be the root of $x$ in $s$. After find with path compression is run on $x$, for every index $i < n$ the node at $i$ in the resulting array keeps its rank from $s$, and its parent is $r$ if $i = p^k(x)$ for some $k \ge 0$, and is its original parent $p(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: The root is reached in fewer parent steps than there are nodes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure with $n$ nodes and parent map $p$, and let $x < n$. Then there is $d < n$ such that $p^d(x)$ is the root of $x$ and $p^k(x)$ is not the root of $x$ for every $k < d$.

results.title: Ranks after linking two nodes of an array
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an array $A$ of union-find nodes, write $\rho_A(i)$ for the rank stored at index $i$ of $A$, or $0$ if $i$ is not an index of $A$. Let $x, y$ be indices of $A$ and let $A'$ be the array obtained from $A$ by the Batteries link by rank of $x$ and $y$. Then for every natural number $i$, $\rho_{A'}(i) = \rho_A(y) + 1$ if $x \ne y$, $\rho_A(x) = \rho_A(y)$ and $i = y$, and $\rho_{A'}(i) = \rho_A(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: Ranks after linking in a union-find structure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, write $\rho(i)$ for the rank of $i$ in $S$ ($0$ if $i$ is not a node of $S$), and let $x, y$ be nodes of $S$ such that $y$ is a root, that is, the parent of $y$ is $y$. Let $S'$ be the result of linking $x$ and $y$ by rank. Then for every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in $S'$ is $\rho(y) + 1$ if $x \ne y$, $\rho(x) = \rho(y)$ and $i = y$, and is $\rho(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: Linking two roots by rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U$ be a union-find structure on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $x, y < n$ be roots of $U$, i.e. each is its own parent. Let $U'$ be obtained by linking $x$ and $y$ by rank: nothing changes if $x = y$; otherwise, if $\operatorname{rank}(y) < \operatorname{rank}(x)$ then $y$ gets parent $x$, and if not then $x$ gets parent $y$ and, when the two ranks are equal, the rank of $y$ increases by one. Then for every…

results.title: Union unfolds to two finds and a link
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U$ be a union-find structure on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $x, y < n$. Run find with path compression on $x$ in $U$, giving a structure $U_1$ and a root $r_x$; then run find on $y$ in $U_1$ (not in $U$), giving a structure $U_2$ and a root $r_y$. Then the node array of the union of $x$ and $y$ in $U$ equals the array obtained from the node array of $U_2$ by linking $r_x$ and $r_y$ by rank: nothing changes if…

results.title: Path compression preserves ranks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x$ a node of $S$, and let $S'$ be the structure returned by FIND on $x$ with path compression. For every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in $S'$ equals the rank of $i$ in $S$, where the rank of an index that is not a node is $0$.

results.title: Ranks after a union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, write $\rho(i)$ for the rank of $i$ in $S$ ($0$ if $i$ is not a node of $S$) and $r(i)$ for the root of $i$ in $S$. For nodes $x, y$ of $S$ and every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in the union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ (union by rank with path compression) is $\rho(r(y)) + 1$ if $r(x) \ne r(y)$, $\rho(r(x)) = \rho(r(y))$ and $r(y) = i$, and is $\rho(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: Linking by rank with operation counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an array $A$ of union-find nodes, each storing a parent index and a rank, and indices $x, y$ of $A$, this computation returns an array together with a count $(t, p, w)$ of rank tests $t$, parent writes $p$ and rank writes $w$. If $x = y$ it returns $A$ with count $(0, 0, 0)$. Otherwise it makes one rank test; if the rank of $y$ is less than the rank of $x$, it sets the parent of $y$ to $x$ (one parent write).…

results.title: Counted linking returns the linked array
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an array $A$ of union-find nodes and indices $x, y$ of $A$, the array returned by counted linking of $x$ and $y$ in $A$ is exactly the array produced by the uncounted Batteries link by rank of $x$ and $y$ in $A$.

results.title: Operation counts of linking by rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an array of union-find nodes, let $x, y$ be indices of $A$, and write $r_x$ and $r_y$ for the ranks stored at $x$ and $y$. Counted linking of $x$ and $y$ in $A$ makes $(t, p, w)$ rank tests, parent writes and rank writes, where $(t, p, w)$ is $(0, 0, 0)$ if $x = y$, is $(1, 1, 0)$ if $x \ne y$ and $r_y < r_x$, is $(2, 1, 1)$ if $x \ne y$ and $r_x = r_y$, and is $(2, 1, 0)$ otherwise, that is, if…

results.title: Union by rank with operation counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, this computation runs counted FIND on $x$ in $S$, giving a structure $S_1$ and a root $r_x$; then counted FIND on $y$ in $S_1$, giving a structure $S_2$ and a root $r_y$; then counted linking of $r_x$ and $r_y$ in the node array of $S_2$. It returns the array produced by the linking, with cost $((a, b), (t, p, w))$, where $a$ and $b$ are the total numbers of…

results.title: Counted union returns the union's array
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, the array returned by the counted union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ equals the node array of the Batteries union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ (union by rank with path compression).

results.title: The FIND phases of a union make two more root tests than parent writes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, in the counted union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ the total number of root tests made by its two FIND calls equals the total number of parent writes they make plus $2$.

results.title: Schnorr verifier's acceptance condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q$ a natural number and $g, y \in G$ (the base and the public key); for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a$ is the representative of $a$ in $\{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ (and $\bar a = |a|$ when $q = 0$, so that $\mathbb{Z}/q = \mathbb{Z}$). The verifier accepts a transcript $(I, r, s)$ with $I \in G$ and $r, s \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ when…

results.title: Schnorr prover's response
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number. For a secret key $x$, prover randomness $k$ and challenge $r$, all in $\mathbb{Z}/q$, the prover's answer is $s = rx + k \in \mathbb{Z}/q$.

results.title: Completeness of the Schnorr identification scheme
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ a natural number and $g \in G$ with $g^q = 1$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For all $x, k, r \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, with public key $y = g^x$, the honest transcript $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ is accepted, that is, $g^{rx + k} (y^r)^{-1} = g^k$.

results.title: Schnorr knowledge extractor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number. For $r, s, r', s' \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ (the challenges and answers of two transcripts), the extracted exponent is $(s - s')(r - r')^{-1} \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, where $u^{-1}$ is the inverse of $u$ in $\mathbb{Z}/q$ when $u$ is a unit (and, otherwise, a conventional element of $\mathbb{Z}/q$ depending on $u$). For $q$ prime and $r \ne r'$ it is $(s - s')/(r - r')$.

results.title: Special soundness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q$ a prime and $g, y \in G$ with $g^q = 1$ and $y^q = 1$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. Let $I \in G$ and $r, s, r', s' \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ with $r \ne r'$, and suppose both transcripts $(I, r, s)$ and $(I, r', s')$ are accepted, that is, $g^s (y^r)^{-1} = I$ and…

results.title: Honest Schnorr transcript
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$; for $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $g^a$ for $g^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a secret key $x$, prover randomness $k$ and challenge $r$, all in $\mathbb{Z}/q$, the honest transcript is the element $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ of $G \times \mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.

results.title: Simulated Schnorr transcript
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g, y \in G$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a challenge $r$ and an answer $s$ in $\mathbb{Z}/q$, the simulated transcript is the element $(g^s (y^r)^{-1}, r, s)$ of $G \times \mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.

results.title: Distribution of honest Schnorr transcripts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$; for $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $g^a$ for $g^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a secret key $x \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, this is the law of the honest transcript $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ when $(k, r)$ is uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.

results.title: Schnorr simulator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g, y \in G$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. The simulator's distribution is the law of the simulated transcript $(g^s (y^r)^{-1}, r, s)$ when $(r, s)$ is uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$; it uses only $g$ and the public key $y$.

results.title: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$ with $g^q = 1$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For every secret key $x \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, with public key $y = g^x$, the honest transcript $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ with $(k, r)$ uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$ has the same distribution as the…
